description: Student team interested in space, physics, computer science, and innovation.
summary:
BRACE is an interactive dashboard that makes NASA’s microgravity combustion research easy to explore. On Earth, hot gas rises and a candle burns as a yellow teardrop. Without gravity, flames become small, blue and spherical, so fire behaves differently and spacecraft fire safety cannot copy Earth practice.

The dashboard brings together 23 investigations, from the Space Shuttle and Mir to the space station, in one searchable, sortable and comparable table, each linked to its NASA source. A range checker shows which experiments tested a given oxygen level, pressure or flow. The page marks missing values as “not confirmed” and separates results from facility design ranges.

A Fire Safety section links 18 findings to the detectors, suppressants, materials tests, ventilation and escape design they inform. Each is labelled Result, In service, Planned or Lesson learned. Examples include nitrogen suppressant strengthening a flame and smoke particles that look different in space.

The Candle Lab lets anyone change gravity, pressure, oxygen, temperature and wind and watch a flame react. It is a simplified teaching model, not measured data.

All content comes from public NASA sources. Next steps are loading raw data from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics archive and adding a plain-English glossary.
details: We created a dashboard to organize and classify data about fire in microgravity. It is interactive, easy to use, and polished. It is intended to help people with their research, and teach them about this topic. We used HTML and Visual Studio Code to create this. We considered the viewer's ability to interact with the website to help them understand the content better.
